assigned_requirements: Input contract: raw location.search string; queryString.parse(search) internally for values; key occurrence order from the raw string; both §5.1 order facts hold in the installed query-string v6.1.0
Key-decoder agreement: raw-string key scan decodes keys with the same decoder queryString.parse v6.1.0 uses
Output contract: camelCase utmSource/utmCampaign/internalRef/utmData; utmData = every other utm_* param excluding exactly utm_source and utm_campaign, keyed by param name, values sanitized

Sanitization rules (D4): repeated param -> first occurrence; 255-char truncation with surrogate-pair-safe tail (fix commit fa51c91a5); utmData cap of 10 keys, first 10 by occurrence order in the raw query string

Absence semantics (§5.1 + §7.2): absent param -> absent/undefined field, no fabricated fallbacks; utmData present only when >=1 additional utm_* param captured; valueless ?utm_source parses to null and passes through as-is
Placement: helper in app/javascript/shared/lib/utils.js alongside standardizeQueryParamsObject; new imports (query-string, decode-uri-component) at top
verified: Input contract: sanitizeTrackingParams(search) at utils.js:42 takes the raw string; utils.js:43 calls queryString.parse(search) for values; utils.js:45-56 derives keysInOccurrenceOrder from queryString.extract(search).split("&") — exactly the mechanism class §5.1 cites. Installed version verified: node_modules/query-string/package.json declares "version": "6.1.0". Order fact 1 verified in node_modules/query-string/index.js: parse() ends in Object.keys(ret).sort().reduce(...) — keys alphabetized unconditionally. Order fact 2 verified: the default (arrayFormat 'none') accumulator assigns the first occurrence then [].concat(accumulator[key], value) for repeats, building arrays in occurrence order; the final reduce's Boolean(value) && typeof value === 'object' && !Array.isArray(value) guard routes arrays to the else branch untouched, so element [0] is the first occurrence. Both §5.1 order facts hold as stated.

Key-decoder agreement: parse v6.1.0 per param does param.replace(/\+/g, ' ').split('='), takes element [0], and passes it to decode() -> decodeComponent (require('decode-uri-component'); options.decode defaults true). The helper's scan (utils.js:50-51) does param.replace(/\+/g, " ").split("=")[0] then decodeUriComponent(rawKey) — identical pre-replacement, identical split, identical decoder. node_modules/query-string/node_modules does not exist, so query-string's require('decode-uri-component') and the helper's import resolve to the same single installed instance (decode-uri-component@0.2.0, verified in node_modules/decode-uri-component/package.json). Adversarial traces (on paper, both pipelines): (1) ?%75tm_source=google&utm_source=bing — both decode %75 -> u, parse accumulates ['google','bing'], helper takes [0]='google'; (2) ?utm%5Fmedium=cpc — both yield key utm_medium, captured in utmData; (3) ?utm_%zz=x — decodeURIComponent throws in both, decode-uri-component's customDecodeURIComponent returns 'utm_%zz' unchanged in both (%zz matches no %[a-f0-9]{2} token), key agrees, captured; (4) ?utm_a+b=1 — both yield key 'utm_a b' (fails the utm_ prefix test identically... n/a: 'utm_a b' does start with utm_ — captured under 'utm_a b' in both); (5) ?utm_source&utm_medium&&utm_source=real — parse yields utm_source: [null,'real'] and utm_medium: null plus a '' key from the empty segment; helper takes utmSource = null (first occurrence, passes through as-is), utmData = {utm_medium: null}; the scan skips the empty segment (utils.js:49) while parse creates ret[''] — divergence is inert: '' can never pass the indexOf("utm_") === 0 filter and is not one of the three named lookups; (6) ?utm_%26x=1 — %26 is not a literal & so neither pipeline splits early; both decode to 'utm_&x', captured identically. No reachable input produces a scan/parse key-set disagreement.

Output contract: utils.js:59-67 assigns utmSource/utmCampaign/internalRef (camelCase) from parsedParams.utm_source/.utm_campaign/.internal_ref; utils.js:69-77 filters keysInOccurrenceOrder to key.indexOf("utm_") === 0 && key !== "utm_source" && key !== "utm_campaign" && parsedParams[key] !== undefined — exactly the §5.1 exclusion of only utm_source and utm_campaign; utmData entries keyed by the decoded param name with sanitizeTrackingValue applied to each value (utils.js:81-84). A literal utm_data URL param would land inside utmData as key 'utm_data' — conforming, since §5.1's exclusion list is exactly the two names.

D4 rule 1 (first occurrence): sanitizeTrackingValue (utils.js:31) isArray(value) ? value[0] : value — valid because v6.1.0 arrays are occurrence-ordered and survive the final sort (verified in library source, above).

D4 rule 2 (255 truncation, surrogate-safe): utils.js:33-38 slice(0, TRACKING_VALUE_MAX_LENGTH=255) then drops a trailing code unit in 0xD800-0xDBFF. Matches fix commit fa51c91a5 verbatim (git show fa51c91a5 — in range, message: lone high surrogate would serialize as bare \udXXX escape and fail the signup POST). Empty-string edge safe: "".charCodeAt(-1) is NaN, both comparisons false, returns "".

D4 rule 3 (10-key cap by occurrence): utils.js:69-77 filter-then-.slice(0, UTM_DATA_MAX_KEYS=10) over keysInOccurrenceOrder — the first 10 QUALIFYING keys by raw-string occurrence order, order never touched by the sorted parse output; dedup via indexOf (utils.js:52-54) pins a repeated key to its first-occurrence position.

Absence semantics: all three top-level fields guarded by parsedParams.<key> !== undefined (parse never stores undefined — valueless becomes null), so absent param -> field never assigned; utmData assigned only inside if (utmDataKeys.length > 0) (utils.js:79) — absent otherwise, no empty-object fabrication; valueless ?utm_source -> parse yields null -> isArray(null) false, isString(null) false -> returned as-is (utils.js:31-32) -> trackingParams.utmSource = null. Zero fabricated fallbacks: no || "", || 0, || [], || {} anywhere in the helper (verified over utils.js:23-88).
Placement: helper block sits immediately after standardizeQueryParamsObject (utils.js:10-21 then 23-88); imports queryString (utils.js:5) and decodeUriComponent (utils.js:6) at top of file.

notes: No findings. Three unreachable-input observations recorded for completeness, none flagged (same unreachability class as settled LOW 4): (1) queryString.extract does not trim() while parse does trim() the whole input — a literal trailing space character in location.search (e.g. '?utm_medium&utm_term ') would give the scan key 'utm_term ' while parse holds 'utm_term', dropping that key from utmData; unreachable because browsers percent-encode spaces in the query component, so location.search never contains a raw space. (2) The lone-high-surrogate drop applies even when no truncation occurred (a <=255-unit value already ending in a lone high surrogate loses its last code unit); unreachable — decode-uri-component cannot emit lone surrogates from percent sequences (decodeURIComponent rejects surrogate ranges; the fallback emits U+FFFD or leaves input verbatim) and browser URL parsing replaces raw lone surrogates before they reach location.search; the drop is also the exact protective intent of fa51c91a5 (an unparsable \udXXX escape would fail the signup POST either way). (3) parse creates a '' key for empty '&&' segments that the scan skips — inert, '' can never qualify for utmData nor collide with the three named lookups. Library facts pinned: query-string 6.1.0 (node_modules/query-string/package.json), parse ends in Object.keys(ret).sort().reduce with the !Array.isArray guard preserving occurrence-ordered arrays (node_modules/query-string/index.js); decode-uri-component 0.2.0 single shared instance (no node_modules/query-string/node_modules). Commits touching utils.js in range: 8dcc2f06f (helper added), 299cf9465 (key scan switched to decode-uri-component), fa51c91a5 (surrogate-safe truncation) — all three land on spec-traceable behavior.
